text:
bob: FYI seeing a p95 latency jump and throughput dip on pool-c after the v7b rollout. Not a full outage but customer-facing p95 up ~120ms.
perf-bot: ALERT: latency_spike pool-c p95 240ms -> 360ms (detected 1912345705) :rotating_light:
carol: thanks — any change in seqlen distribution or batching?
bob: Seq len tail increased slightly (more 1024+ requests), but traffic shape unchanged from last three hours. Throughput down ~18%.
greg: I pulled flamegraphs from the nodes in pool-c. Short summary: kernel selection is spending way more time in the new attention kernel variant. KV cache hit-rate down ~9% on hot prefixes.
maya: could tokenizer subtoken boundaries have changed? v7b included a subtokenizer tweak that can split prefixes differently. If prefixes misalign, KV cache lookups may miss and we re-run more decode work.
carol: can you paste the top lines from the profile?
greg: sure — snippet from sampled profiler (30s window):
```
samples: 1000
kernel_select() 45% -> 72%  (+27pp)
batch_dispatch() 18% -> 26%  (+8pp)
attention_kernel_new() 12% -> 38% (+26pp)
kv_cache.lookup_miss 6% -> 18% (+12pp)
cpu_wait_io 3% -> 1%
```
carol: oh — attention_kernel_new skyrocketed. That suggests our kernel selector chose an unfriendly kernel for the new tokenization patterns.
bob: what's the selector heuristic? sequence length + tok-density + hardware flags, right?
greg: yes. The new subtoken splits increased average per-step token variance; the selector preferred the new kernel for mid-length batches but perf regressess when KV misses force longer recompute.
maya: quick test idea — pin kernel to legacy for a single host and run replay. If perf stays good -> selector rules need patch.
carol: agree. Also try replaying requests with old tokenizer on v7b runtime to see if subtokenization is the cause. If KV miss delta persists, it's tokenizer.
infra-bot: deploy-canary created: canary-host-7b-1 (pool-c) at 1912346000.
bob: ran a quick A/B: pinned legacy kernel on canary-host-7b-1, p95 dropped back to baseline within 3 minutes. KV hit-rate improved ~7pp.
maya: so two vectors: (1) tokenizer changed prefix boundaries causing KV fragmentation, (2) kernel selector misrouted to new kernel that behaves poorly when kv miss rate increases. Both amplify each other.
carol: immediate mitigation: 1) revert kernel selector heuristic to prefer legacy kernel for mid-size batches in pool-c, 2) rollback tokenizer subtokenizer tweak for v7b rollout (canary pause).
greg: I'll open a perf regression issue and include flamegraphs — INC-4721 created.
bob: rolling back tokenizer option on remaining hosts now. Patch in staging set to v7a-subtokenizer.
perf-bot: ROUTING CHANGE applied: kernel_selector heuristics overridden on pool-c at 1912347200.
infra-bot: rollback completed for tokenizer flag on 6/7 hosts at 1912348200 — final host draining.
maya: follow-ups: (a) add KV prefix alignment test to rollout checklist, (b) extend kernel selector to consider recent KV miss rate as a factor, (c) add synthetic replay with borderline seqlen tails.
carol: I'll file the selector follow-up and assign to eng-runtime. Also add a small regression unit test for tokenizer->kv alignment.
bob: closing loop — metrics back to normal post-rollback, throughput recovered. Will keep canary running for 2h.
greg: attaching full flamegraph and raw profile to INC-4721.
carol: nice triage everyone. Extra: note to docs — include note about tokenizer changes and KV cache compatibility in rollout runbook. :memo:
bob: thanks — marking thread resolved unless we see further spikes. :white_check_mark:
